solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Obstruct major route in Sweden yet to be built

indicators.note: says the motorway sits inside the other letters

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

indicators.note: something yet to be built still has to be put together, so these letters get assembled in a new order

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI as letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that a big Swedish road project has stalled before construction even began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be built' rearranges the letters as TYE; 'in' sets the motorway inside. The M1 is Britain's main motorway, London to Leeds; 'major' looks like an adjective, not part of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie someone is to thwart or block their plans, a close synonym of obstruct.

clue.text: Fighter shunning society is defamatory about battle site

indicators.note: the fighter takes the place of the society it avoids, so one letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: someone who is defamatory about another slanders them
F labels fighter aircraft, as in the F-16

explanation.surface: A soldier who avoids company is accused of badmouthing the place where a battle was fought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shunning' swaps the S at the front of SLANDERS for F, the fighter-plane letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders, in Belgium, saw some of the bloodiest fighting of the First World War, notably around Ypres.

clue.text: Recover chapter introducing novels ace composed

indicators.note: the chapter letter comes first, leading in the other letters
composed means arranged or put together, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: An author gets back on their feet as a new chapter starts a run of well-written novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like a description of the novels but is the signal to rearrange; 'introducing' puts C at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to regain health after illness, gradually getting better.

clue.text: Some sedentary ex-PM

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following word are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is described as rather inactive.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was the British prime minister from 1955 to 1957, resigning after the Suez crisis.

clue.text: Cook top citrous food from a deli?

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to prepare a lemony dish bought at a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a kitchen verb but signals the rearrangement of TOP CITROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosciutto is Italian dry-cured ham, a typical sliced item at a delicatessen counter; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: American hotel visitors not half getting fever

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the opening three of its six letters

parts.note: people staying at a hotel are its guests

explanation.surface: Half the American guests at a hotel have come down with a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps GUE of GUESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering fits.

clue.text: Impression from a malleable element in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: places these letters inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
tin is a soft metallic element easily shaped

explanation.surface: A mark left by a soft metal somewhere in Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' here is the sense of outward appearance, not a dent or a mimicry.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a surface sheen, and figuratively an outward appearance, as in a patina of respectability.

clue.text: Excitedly log a grey medieval church ornament

indicators.note: excited things move about wildly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A log of grey stone is eagerly carved into decoration for an old church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excitedly' rearranges LOG A GREY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a grotesque carved waterspout typical of medieval church architecture.

clue.text: Lofty group of nuns has difficult assignment

parts.note: lofty means tall
nuns belong to a religious order

explanation.surface: A towering religious community has been handed a hard task.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demand that is unreasonably hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Man ironically greeted when touring area with a tropical fruit

indicators.note: the greeting goes round the area letter, as a tourist goes round a place

parts.note: guv, short for governor, is a jokey or mock-deferential way of greeting a man

explanation.surface: A man greeted with irony while travelling round a region carrying fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when touring' puts GUV around A; another A follows. GUV is British slang for a boss or any man, often said tongue in cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a pear-shaped fruit grown in tropical regions.

clue.text: Chap carrying voguish quartet from Rome in people carrier

indicators.note: the word for chap holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a chap is a man
in means fashionable
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A man takes four fashionable Romans in his family car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' signals one piece holding the others. People carrier is the British term for a passenger van.
explanation.definitionFit: A minivan is a small van-shaped passenger vehicle, the US term for what Britons call a people carrier.

clue.text: Apparent area of religious significance with noted dynasty

parts.note: a see is the district under a bishop's authority
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: A sacred region evidently linked to a famous ruling house.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming means outwardly appearing so, which is what apparent means in the sense of ostensible.

clue.text: Pioneering female is drawn for the most part

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, all but its last letter

parts.note: a game that is drawn is even, neither side ahead

explanation.surface: A trailblazing woman is mostly depicted in drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of EVEN. 'drawn' tempts as sketched, but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve was, in the Bible, the first woman, so the pioneer of her sex.

clue.text: Top film star gained ally at work after embracing director

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the director letter
something at work is in operation, so these letters are set going in a new order

explanation.surface: A movie star made a friend at the studio once she took on the director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges GAINED ALLY; 'embracing' then wraps it around D.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading lady is the actress with the main female role, the top billing in a film.

clue.text: Legal case supported by place with a new strategy

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits on top of the rest, held up by it

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A lawsuit backed by a fresh venue, with a plan of attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An action plan is a scheme of concrete steps to reach a goal, a kind of strategy.

clue.text: See golf shot played with tee at end flying off? Indication of fear, maybe

indicators.note: a shot that is played is set in motion, so the letters are shuffled
the letter at the end of the word goes, as a tee flies away when a ball is struck

parts.note: spelling out the letter T

explanation.surface: Watch a golf drive where the tee shoots off at the end, perhaps a scary moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tee at end flying off' drops the final T of SHOT; 'played' rearranges SEE GOLF SHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose bumps, the prickled skin raised by cold or fright, are one sign of fear, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: On a regular basis, Roman's first location for finding water

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: A Roman explains where he first found water, routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a regular basis' takes the second, fourth and every other letter of ROMANS FIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where water is found.

clue.text: Event in grounds

definitions.meaning: cause or reason, grounds for doing something

explanation.surface: An event held in some parkland.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasion means both a notable happening and a reason, as in no occasion for alarm.

clue.text: Sound mildly disapproving of bend in motorcycle event

indicators.note: the bend letter sits inside the race letters

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race
a U-bend, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Someone clicks their tongue at a curve on a motorbike race course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut at something is to make the clicking noise of mild annoyance.

clue.text: Old story about very limited Greek product

indicators.note: the story wraps around the letter for very

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
very cut down to its abbreviation, V

explanation.surface: An ancient tale about an export from Greece with little to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside LIE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives and their oil are among Greece's best-known exports.

clue.text: Where one might find boozing with large drinks accompaniment virtually open to view?

parts.note: drinking goes on in a pub

indicators.note: virtually means nearly, so the word falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: ice is added to drinks

explanation.surface: Where heavy drinking with lots of ice happens almost openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims ICE to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in public means in full view of others, open to view.

clue.text: US actress ruined the mood largely? That's uncomfortably true

parts.note: Glenn Close is an American actress

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: An American star spoiled the atmosphere, and the remark hit a nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts MOOD to MOO; 'ruined' rearranges THE MOO as TO HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark close to home touches a sensitive point because it is uncomfortably accurate.

clue.text: One's first line of goods has something with zest?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a range is a line of products

explanation.surface: A firm's leading product line has some lively item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zest' tempts as enthusiasm, but here it is citrus peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the outer peel of citrus fruit, so an orange is one thing that has it.

clue.text: Select for audience film

indicators.note: the word is as heard by listeners, so its sound matters

parts.note: to select is to pick

explanation.surface: Choose a movie for the viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for audience' gives the sound of PICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Pic is informal for a picture, a motion picture, or film.

clue.text: Hear Yankee describing a memorable song?

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Listen to an American with a tune that sticks in the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune is one that is instantly appealing and easily remembered.

clue.text: Lead place for retreat in recently formed company

parts.note: the lead in a show is its star

indicators.note: retreating goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to place is to put

explanation.surface: A main role found in a quiet hideaway for a new business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retreat' turns PUT into TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is a newly launched business, often a small tech venture.

clue.text: Fail abysmally in military vehicle

definitions.meaning: to ... is to flop badly, as a film ... at the box office

explanation.surface: Breaking down hopelessly inside an army vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tank is both slang for a dismal failure and the armoured vehicle of land warfare.

clue.text: Old king's one objection to fish

parts.note: Hal was the familiar name of Henry V, a king of England
I is the Roman numeral one
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch raises a single objection to the fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of king's stands for 'has', linking HAL to I.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: Wound the feelings of English actor

definitions.meaning: John ... was an English actor known for The Elephant Man

explanation.surface: Upsetting a British performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt is both a verb for causing emotional pain and the surname of the actor John Hurt.

clue.text: Feature in a church newspaper

definitions.meaning: a pipe ... is a fixture of many churches
a publication that speaks for a group, such as a party paper

explanation.surface: A regular column in a church newsletter.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ names both the musical instrument in a church and a mouthpiece publication.

clue.text: Rock band most hear mistakenly around middle of gig

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the central letter
letters taken mistakenly are in the wrong order, so they are reshuffled
only the centre letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Most of the crowd mishear a rock group in the middle of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges MOST HEAR; 'around' puts it around I, the middle of GIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerosmith is an American hard rock band formed in Boston in 1970.
